# Proverbs 13 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A-son wise — discipline-of a-father; but-a-scoffer does-not-hear rebuke.

**2** From-[the]-fruit-of [the]-mouth-of a-man he-eats good, but-[the]-soul-of [the]-treacherous [eats] violence.

**3** One-guarding his-mouth keeps his-soul; one-opening-wide his-lips — destruction for-him.

**4** Craving but-there-is-not — [the]-soul-of [the]-sluggard; but-[the]-soul-of [the]-diligent is-made-fat.

**5** A-word-of falsehood [the]-righteous hates, but-[the]-wicked acts-shamefully and-disgracefully.

**6** Righteousness guards [the one]-blameless-of way, but-wickedness overthrows [the]-sinner.

**7** There-is one-making-himself-rich and-there-is-nothing at-all; one-making-himself-poor and-wealth [is] great.

**8** Ransom-of a-man's life [is] his-riches, but-a-poor-man does-not-hear rebuke.

**9** Light-of [the]-righteous rejoices, but-[the]-lamp-of [the]-wicked is-extinguished.

**10** Only by-pride one-gives strife, but-with [those]-taking-counsel [is] wisdom.

**11** Wealth from-vanity will-diminish, but-one-gathering by-hand will-increase.

**12** Hope deferred makes-sick [the]-heart, but-a-tree-of life [is] desire [when]-it-comes.

**13** One-despising a-word will-be-pledged to-it, but-one-fearing a-commandment — he will-be-rewarded.

**14** Teaching-of [the]-wise [is] a-fountain-of life, to-turn-away from-snares-of death.

**15** Good understanding gives favor, but-[the]-way-of [the]-treacherous [is] enduring.

**16** Every prudent-one acts with-knowledge, but-a-fool spreads-out folly.

**17** A-messenger wicked falls into-evil, but-a-messenger faithful [brings] healing.

**18** Poverty and-shame [come to] one-ignoring discipline, but-one-keeping correction will-be-honored.

**19** Desire fulfilled is-sweet to-[the]-soul, but-[an]-abomination to-fools [is] to-turn-from evil.

**20** One-walking with wise-ones will-be-wise, but-a-companion-of fools will-suffer-harm.

**21** Evil pursues sinners, but-[the]-righteous [are]-repaid [with] good.

**22** A-good-[man] leaves-an-inheritance to-sons'-sons, but-stored-up for-[the]-righteous [is the]-wealth-of [the]-sinner.

**23** Much food [is in the]-fallow-ground-of [the]-poor, but-there-is one-swept-away for-lack-of justice.

**24** One-withholding his-rod hates his-son, but-one-loving-him seeks-him-early [with]-discipline.

**25** [The]-righteous eats to-[the]-satisfying-of his-soul, but-[the]-belly-of [the]-wicked will-lack.

---
## EMET Literal Notes

- **13:7**: Remarkable observation on the gap between appearance and reality in wealth. Possibly the earliest commentary on conspicuous consumption.

- **13:12**: Tocheleth memushakah — 'hope drawn out/deferred.' One of the most psychologically astute observations in ancient literature.

- **13:24**: Chosekh shivto — 'one withholding his rod.' The rod (shevet) is the shepherd's instrument — guidance, not brutality.

— EMET
